text: The watcher runs on its own proved protocol, `factory/protocol`, which the factory built from #9 and merged as #11. The root module imports it through a `replace` line. Before each step the watcher takes on an issue, it maps the issue onto the model as it is and as the step would leave it, and takes the step only if the model has it. Proposal and lock hashes and commit SHAs are renamed onto the model's few values, keeping every comparison a step makes. A refused step labels the issue for a person. Wiring it in showed three steps the watcher took that the model didn't have: a build that stops before it makes a pull request, a build that fails its own gate, and a pull request that passes CI but can't merge. #13 amended `factory/protocol` to add them, with @gitdek's answers: a writer's retry builds a stopped build again and counts its stops afresh, and solve or revise draft again after one. So each failed post now records why it failed. The watcher counts stopped builds from its own posts, not from its build logs. A build the factory itself stopped partway through becomes a stop it posts, instead of another agent run.
